newsitem.title: USA: Schlumberger sees offsetting Q3 items.
newsitem.headline: Schlumberger sees offsetting Q3 items.

text.p: Schlumberger Ltd said Monday it will report a third quarter credit and offsetting charges, and talked about future staff cuts and writeoffs.
Chief Financial Officer Arthur Lindenauer stated, "Over the near term these items will have no material impact on the results of Schlumberger."

With increasing profitability and strong outlook in the U.S., Schlumberger said, it will recognize a portion of the U.S. income tax benefit related to its U.S. subsidiary's tax loss carryforwards and all temporary differences. This will result in a credit of $360 million.
It said there will be an after tax charge of $300 million related primarily to Electricity and Gas Management, and Geco-Prakla.
In addition, Schlumberger will record a charge of $58 million after tax including a loss on the divestiture of its remaining defense-related activity, certain asset impairments, and other charges.

Within the Measurement & Systems business segment, the company said, the Electricity and Gas Management product lines have been combined into a single business to more efficiently serve the rapidly changing energy supply sector.
It said tyhis will result in lower headcount and fewer manufacturing facilities and products, but no one was immediately available to provide details.

Within the Oilfield Services segment, Schlumberger said, the much improved results of Geco-Prakla in the quarter are mostly due to the Marine activity. The losses in the Land and Transition Zone businesses have been reduced, "but we are convinced that more radical changes, including the write-off of Land goodwill, are required to ensure the long-term financial health of these businesses."
